accounts_gmail_limit_modal_title.description: Modal title explaining Gmail single-account limitation

accounts_gmail_limit_modal_body.message:
Chrome provides a built-in sign-in API that extensions use to access Gmail. This API only allows one Google account per browser profile. It is a browser-level restriction, not a choice.

To support multiple accounts, a backend server would be needed to handle Google's authentication. That would mean your email data passes through someone else's server. That is not something this extension will ever do.

If Google changes their API to support multiple accounts without a server (like Microsoft already does for Outlook), this limitation will be removed.

In the meantime, multiple Gmail accounts can be used by creating separate Chrome profiles, or by connecting additional accounts via IMAP through InboxBridge.

security_hero_subtitle.message: This page describes what the extension does and does not do with your information. No claims to verify, just facts to read.

security_accessed_description.message: The only data the extension reads
security_accessed_description.description: Security section: what is accessed subtitle

security_accessed_verification_detail.message: Only emails containing verification codes or magic links are read. All other emails are ignored entirely.

security_accessed_readonly_detail.message: Email content is read but never modified, deleted, or moved. The extension cannot compose, send, or alter any email.

security_accessed_local_detail.message: All email parsing happens on your device. Email content is processed in memory and never leaves the browser.

security_stored_description.message: Everything saved locally, and nothing else
security_stored_description.description: Security section: what is stored subtitle

security_stored_connection_detail.message: Which email accounts are connected and whether the connection is active. No email content is stored.

security_stored_preferences_detail.message: Display settings, blocked domains, and automation preferences. Stored in Chrome's local encrypted storage.

security_stored_cache_detail.message: Recently detected verification codes are held briefly so they can be offered for autofill. They expire automatically and can be cleared from Settings at any time.

security_notdone_title.description: Security section: what is not done

security_notdone_description.message: Things the extension will never do
security_notdone_description.description: Security section: what is not done subtitle

security_notdone_analytics_detail.message: No usage analytics, no event tracking, no telemetry of any kind. There is nothing to opt out of because nothing is collected.

security_notdone_connections_title.description: Security fact: no external connections title

security_notdone_connections_detail.message: The extension does not contact any server, API, or service other than your email provider. It does not phone home.
security_notdone_connections_detail.description: Security fact: no external connections detail

security_notdone_data_title.description: Security fact: no data leaves title

security_notdone_data_detail.message: Nothing is uploaded, synced, or transmitted anywhere. All data stays in your browser's local storage on your machine.
security_notdone_data_detail.description: Security fact: no data leaves detail

security_perm_identity_reason.message: Signs in with your Google account so verification emails can be read.

security_perm_tabs_reason.message: Detects login and verification pages so codes can be offered for autofill.

security_perm_activetab_reason.message: Checks the current tab for code input fields so verification codes can be inserted.

security_perm_storage_reason.message: Saves preferences and settings locally in Chrome's encrypted storage.

security_perm_scripting_reason.message: Places the autofill chip on login pages so codes can be inserted into form fields.

security_perm_nativemessaging_reason.message: Communicates with the local InboxBridge helper for IMAP accounts. Only active if installed.

security_source_cta_title.message: Words are cheap. Code is proof.

security_source_cta_detail.message: The full source code is on GitHub. Read it, build it, verify every claim.

about_devnote_p1.message: I built InboxKey because I was tired of switching between tabs to copy verification codes. It sounds small, but it interrupts your flow dozens of times a week.

about_devnote_p2.message: Email access is sensitive. I know that. That is exactly why everything is open-source, runs locally, and will never phone home. You should not have to trust a stranger with your inbox. You should be able to verify.

about_support_body.message: InboxKey is free and always will be. A coffee keeps development going and lets me know someone out there finds it useful. Thank you.

about_support_optional.message: Totally optional. Never nags, never blocks features.
